purpose: Compare static, request-dynamic, and DAG-aware routing under one, two, and four objectives without changing the original routing scope.

evidence_roles.request_routing: empirical replay on 419 tasks x 5 models x 3 repeats
evidence_roles.dag_routing: mechanism simulation built from empirical node outcomes; not end-to-end semantic DAG evidence

objectives.multi: maximize 0.45 quality + 0.20 cost efficiency + 0.15 latency efficiency + 0.20 reliability

regimes.static: one fold-training-optimal model for every held-out task
regimes.dynamic: request-feature OOF prediction of every objective component, then per-task selection
regimes.oracle: held-out per-task ex-post upper bound; never a deployable policy
regimes.dag_static: one fold-training-optimal model for every node
regimes.dag_dynamic: independent OOF dynamic choice at each node
regimes.dag_adaptive: OOF dynamic choice plus one retry with the next-ranked model after an empirical failure

cross_validation: shared KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=20260902) over tasks
features: fold-local word TF-IDF(1,2) plus character TF-IDF(3,5), request-time fields only

dag_replay.construction: deterministic groups of four held-out empirical tasks
dag_replay.quality: mean node quality, zero for an unrecovered failed node
dag_replay.success: all nodes reliable and quality >= 0.6 after optional retry

uncertainty: 10000 paired task bootstrap samples; DAG bootstrap uses workflow as unit
primary_comparisons: dynamic minus static for each objective cardinality
oracle minus static headroom for each objective cardinality
DAG adaptive minus DAG dynamic success and utility, with cost and critical-path latency deltas
integrity: no gold answers or outcome labels in router features
all preprocessing fitted inside outer folds
same folds for every regime and objective
simulation claims kept separate from empirical request-routing claims
